delisted effective March&nbsp;6, 2009. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In assessing the director independence, the Board has affirmatively determined that
both members of the Nominating/Corporate Governance Committee: Michael A. Miles and Herbert J. Siegel (who served through May&nbsp;22, 2009); all members the Audit Committee: Michael J. Regan, Thomas V. Reifenheiser, and Wayne T. Smith; and all
three individuals who have served on the compensation committee: Michael A. Miles, Herbert J. Siegel (who served through May&nbsp;22, 2009) and Wayne T. Smith, each qualify as &#147;independent&#148; under NYSE&#146;s and the SEC&#146;s corporate
governance rules, and that our Chairman and CEO, Farid Suleman, does not qualify as &#147;independent&#148; under either set of rules. In making its determination regarding the independence of each of those directors under applicable rules, the
Board of Directors considered each of the relationships identified under Item&nbsp;13. &#147;Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence&#148; and, with respect to the members of the nominating/corporate governance
committee, audit committee and compensation committee, discussed under &#147;The Nominating/Corporate Governance Committee,&#148; &#147;The Audit Committee&#148; and &#147;The Compensation Committee&#148; above. With respect to each person
identified as independent, the Board of Directors determined that those relationships do not affect the individual&#146;s independence because, as applicable, he or she has not made any commitment to the affiliated partnerships of FL&amp;Co. and
none of the rights of an advisory board member or of a special limited partner or of service on the board of directors of a Forstmann Little&nbsp;&amp; Co. affiliate are contingent in any way on or affected by his or her continued service as a
director or member of our Board of Directors. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Board Leadership Structure </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Board believes that the Company&#146;s CEO is best situated to serve as Chairman of the Board because he is the director most familiar
with the Company&#146;s business operations and industry challenges. He is the director that is most capable of effectively identifying strategic opportunities, setting Company priorities and leading the discussion and execution of the
Company&#146;s overall corporate strategy. Independent directors have different perspectives and roles on strategy development and provide a diverse point of view is assisting the Company to evaluate and achieve its goals. The Company&#146;s
independent directors bring experience, oversight and expertise from outside the company and from both inside and outside the media industry, while the CEO brings company-specific experience and expertise. The Board believes that the combined role
of Chairman and CEO provides the best overall strategy development and execution and provides for greater information flow between management and the Board. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The audit committee has adopted policies and procedures requiring audit committee review and approval in advance of all particular engagements for services provided by the Company&#146;s independent
registered public accountants. Prior to rendering any audit and non-audit professional services, Deloitte&nbsp;&amp; Touche LLP discusses such services with the audit committee, and the committee pre-approves the scope of such services and the
related estimated fees. The scope of all audit and non-audit services rendered by Deloitte&nbsp;&amp; Touche LLP during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 was pre-approved by the audit committee. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">During the approval process, the audit committee considers the impact of the scope of services and the related fees on the independence of
